newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU may take France to court over biofuels tax.
newsitem.headline: EU may take France to court over biofuels tax.

text.p: The European Commission may decide on Wednesday to take France to the European Court of Justice over tax breaks for French biofuels on the grounds that they discriminate against similar European products.
A Commission source said European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler was disappointed that the French government had not lived up to its commitment to extend the tax breaks to imported biofuels.
But his two French colleagues, Research Commissioner Edith Cresson and Yves-Thibault de Silguy who is in charge of monetary affairs, were trying to win a tactical delay, the source said.
In December the Commission blocked the scheme designed to encourage the use of fuels derived from crops grown on French land.

France promised in April to change the tax rules, but has told the Commission since then that it was unable to do so because of the change in government following the recent general elections which resulted in victory for Socialist leader Lionel Jospin.
"Fischler proposes to go to court because the old rules will again apply to the present crop," the source said.
The International Energy Agency estimated last year that the cost of the French scheme to support biofuel production could reach two billion francs by the end of the century.
